engineering_decisions.choice: Retain delivery lineage and enforce permitted input cutoffs.
Supply a compatible median method with reference arithmetic and rounding.
Enforce the accepted order input grain after Q1.

support_questions.question: Must the orders relation for day 076 retain 699 raw rows or expose 437 distinct records before the unchanged reference queries run?
support_questions.reason: The supplied documentation identifies repeated export as a data issue but does not define reference input deduplication.
options: Raw rows with the data issue recorded.
Exact-repeat exclusion in a derived input, if required by acceptance.

findings.title: The README defines cal and the date alias.
findings.method: Search every UTF-8 original dataset file for the word cal. Exclude explore_data.py. Extract c.<column> from each KPI SQL string.
findings.impact: 23 KPI definitions directly need cal. revenue_daily also needs it. Loading the CSV with its original date name does not meet the SQL interface.
findings.confidence: High: explicit source rule and complete local search.
options: Expose an in-memory or future loader alias named d.
Expose a future relation or adapter that preserves all calendar columns. Do not change the reference SQL.

findings.title: Calendar coverage meets the documented 90-day input period.
findings.method: Parse ISO dates; compare the set with each date from minimum to maximum; check day_idx sequence and all numbered manifest dates.
findings.impact: No date gap or duplicate explains the cal failure. Morning 91 uses drop 90. The initial CRM history is outside the calendar by design.
findings.confidence: High: all 90 calendar rows and 90 dated manifests checked.
options: Use the supplied date and month boundaries.
Do not add day 000 or morning 91 to business-date coverage without a new requirement.

findings.title: The raw CRM event schema omits the delivery field used by lead_fact.
findings.method: Compare every CRM event header. Execute the original lead_fact definition against the raw event columns in an isolated memory database.
findings.impact: The view query fails with no such column: x.drop_day. Event time cannot replace delivery time.
findings.confidence: High: header scan and SQL failure reproduced.
options: Retain manifest drop_day and source row coordinates in a future ingestion layer.
Use folder numbers only after checking their agreement with manifests. Apply the documented cutoff before building facts.

findings.title: One correction arrives six days late and changes earlier revenue after it becomes available.
findings.method: Group value_corrected rows by lead; compare delivery date with event date; run the original lead_fact select at event cutoffs 63,64,69,70,90 in memory.
findings.impact: L02045 changes from 27,300,000 to 15,000,000 toman. Morning reports 65 through 70 must not use this correction. It first becomes available in morning 71. revenue_daily assigns it to the won date, 2026-09-24.
findings.confidence: High: complete correction scan and target-lead SQL checks.
options: Preserve the original morning cutoff when reproducing a report.
A later report can reflect the correction on the original won date under the reference SQL. Do not overwrite a prior report as part of this task.

findings.title: The supplied rows do not test multiple-correction precedence.
findings.method: Count correction rows per lead and per lead/drop. Inspect all event fields and the ORDER BY clause.
findings.impact: There is one correction and no observed tie. Same-drop corrections with different values would have no documented secondary order. at is an effective event timestamp, not proof of correction issue order.
findings.confidence: High for the absence of observed ties; the intended tied-case behavior is unknown.
options: Detect and report a tied correction if one occurs.
Do not use row position, value size, or at as business precedence without evidence. Seek a support rule only if a real or required tied case remains.

findings.title: The local SQLite build lacks the required median aggregate.
findings.method: Call median in the unmodified local SQLite connection. Compare an isolated diagnostic aggregate, a ranked SQL middle-row average, and pandas on the same Julian-day samples.
findings.impact: Nine KPI definitions cannot run in the unmodified connection. All 806 observed KPI/date groups agree after SQLite rounding when their input expressions stay the same.
findings.confidence: High for the tested SQLite build and supplied data. PostgreSQL equivalence was not executed.
options: Register a compatible aggregate in a future SQLite connection.
Use a ranked SQL calculation in an approved execution adapter.
Use an external local calculation that preserves SQL filters, NULLs, expressions, and rounding. No option is selected.

findings.title: Equivalent median selection does not guarantee equivalent timestamp arithmetic or rounding.
findings.method: Compare SQLite julianday differences with Python datetime differences; apply final SQLite ROUND in both paths. Test empty, all-NULL, odd, even, mixed-NULL, negative, and fractional samples.
findings.impact: Native datetime arithmetic changes 8 KPI/date outputs across the repeated FRT definitions and complaint resolution. Rounding with Python can also differ. The final delivery-days formula divides by 24 before final rounding.
findings.confidence: High: actual rounded differences and boundary experiments retained.
options: Preserve the reference Julian-day expression and SQLite rounding.
Require explicit parity evidence before any engine or timestamp method change.

findings.title: One delivery contains 262 extra exact order rows.
findings.method: Count full-row tuples and order_id groups across all order deliveries. Record every duplicate row path and line. Compare business-key groups with exact-row groups.
findings.impact: There are 37,851 raw rows and 37,589 order IDs. All duplicate keys have identical source values. All 262 extra rows occur within day 076; there are no cross-day order duplicates.
findings.confidence: High: complete scan, row locations, and matching manifest count.
options: Retain the raw rows as evidence.
Treat repeated-export origin as a hypothesis; source generator logs are not supplied.

findings.title: Raw order joins inflate both payments and refund subtraction.
findings.method: Compute paid event gross with Python counters and independent SQLite joins. Repeat with full-row DISTINCT only inside the diagnostic query. Repeat the B2C paid-minus-refunded expression.
findings.impact: Gross rises by 347,454,000 toman with raw order rows. Refund subtraction rises by 15,394,000 toman. The B2C net diagnostic difference is 332,060,000 toman. The input relation to the authoritative SQL needs an acceptance rule.
findings.confidence: High for the diagnostic sums; accepted deduplication behavior is unknown.
options: Confirm that the reference orders relation contains raw rows.
Confirm that exact repeated exports must be excluded from the reference input. Preserve the source and reference SQL in either case.

findings.title: order_fact removes repeated keys after the join, but raw-order KPIs still count them.
findings.method: Count left-join rows before and after a full-row DISTINCT diagnostic; count grouped order_fact rows. Scan event tuples and order/event keys.
findings.impact: The raw left join produces 146,054 rows versus 145,027 in the diagnostic. GROUP BY order_id returns 37,589 rows. MAX event timestamps stay the same for current exact duplicates. COUNT on orders and the damage-category ticket/orders join can still be inflated.
findings.confidence: High for current exact duplicates. Conflicting future order versions are not tested.
options: Keep distinct event types for an order.
Do not remove event rows just because the same order_id occurs more than once. Inspect future conflicting order versions separately.

findings.title: The day 066 support gap is followed by dated records in day 067.
findings.method: Compare expected source files with each manifest and directory. Group support rows dated 2026-09-26 by their actual delivery drop.
findings.impact: Day 067 contains 104 tickets, 229 ticket events, and 25 CSAT rows dated day 066. They are unavailable for morning 67 and available for morning 68. Event-date-only reconstruction would leak these rows into morning 67. Completeness against an independent source total is not known.
findings.confidence: High for missing files and delivered rows; full source completeness is unknown.
options: Report the unavailable source and NULL affected values as required by the README.
Retain delivery metadata when later records arrive. Do not infer a zero from a missing file.

findings.title: Two support timestamp columns change at day 082.
findings.method: Compare every delivered CSV header. Count rows under each changed schema. Use aliases only within the temporary median experiment.
findings.impact: tickets.created_at becomes create_time for 745 rows. ticket_events.at becomes event_time for 1,692 rows. Ignoring the new fields loses support times and can bias medians, backlog, SLA, and damage-rate metrics.
options: Use a version-aware alias adapter in a future loader.
Detect the source columns and expose the established reference names. Keep original names and provenance.

queries.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT c.d, c.jmonth, c.day_in_month, c.mdays, SUM(r.b2c + r.b2b) OVER (PARTITION BY c.jmonth ORDER BY c.d) cum FROM cal c JOIN revenue_daily r USING(d)) SELECT m.d, ROUND(100.0*m.cum/(t.target_million_toman*1e6*m.day_in_month/m.mdays),1) value FROM m JOIN monthly_targets t ON t.jmonth=m.jmonth AND t.scope='ORG'
SELECT c.d, COUNT(o.order_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN orders o ON date(o.created_at)=c.d GROUP BY c.d

WITH cl AS (SELECT lead_id, COALESCE(won_at,lost_at) closed_at, ((julianday(first_contact_at)-julianday(created_at))*24<=24 AND (julianday(proposal_at)-julianday(qualified_at))*24<=120 AND (julianday(COALESCE(won_at,lost_at))-julianday(proposal_at))*24<=720) ok FROM lead_fact WHERE COALESCE(won_at,lost_at) IS NOT NULL) SELECT c.d, ROUND(100.0*AVG(cl.ok),1) value FROM cal c JOIN cl ON date(cl.closed_at) BETWEEN date(c.d,'-6 day') AND c.d GROUP BY c.d

WITH cl AS (SELECT COALESCE(won_at,lost_at) closed_at, won_at IS NOT NULL won FROM lead_fact WHERE COALESCE(won_at,lost_at) IS NOT NULL) SELECT c.d, ROUND(100.0*AVG(cl.won),1) value FROM cal c JOIN cl ON date(cl.closed_at) BETWEEN date(c.d,'-29 day') AND c.d GROUP BY c.d
SELECT c.d, COUNT(l.lead_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN lead_fact l ON date(l.proposal_at) <= c.d AND (COALESCE(l.won_at,l.lost_at) IS NULL OR date(COALESCE(l.won_at,l.lost_at)) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d
SELECT c.d, ROUND(SUM(r.b2b) OVER (PARTITION BY c.jmonth ORDER BY c.d)/1e6,1) value FROM cal c JOIN revenue_daily r USING(d)

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.task_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN task_fact t ON t.team_id='T_ENT' AND t.due_date < c.d AND date(t.created_at) <= c.d AND (t.done_at IS NULL OR date(t.done_at) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d

WITH x AS (SELECT date d, SUM(spend_toman) s, SUM(leads) l FROM mkt_daily GROUP BY 1) SELECT c.d, ROUND(SUM(x.s)/NULLIF(SUM(x.l),0)/1000.0,0) value FROM cal c JOIN x ON x.d BETWEEN date(c.d,'-6 day') AND c.d GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.task_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN task_fact t ON t.team_id='T_DIG' AND t.due_date < c.d AND date(t.created_at) <= c.d AND (t.done_at IS NULL OR date(t.done_at) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.task_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN task_fact t ON t.team_id='T_MKT' AND t.due_date < c.d AND date(t.created_at) <= c.d AND (t.done_at IS NULL OR date(t.done_at) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(o.order_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN order_fact o ON o.paid_at <= c.d||' 22:00:00' AND (o.cancelled_at IS NULL OR o.cancelled_at > c.d||' 22:00:00') AND (o.picked_at IS NULL OR o.picked_at > c.d||' 22:00:00') GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, ROUND(100.0*COALESCE(t.n,0)/o.n,2) value FROM cal c JOIN (SELECT date(delivered_at) d, COUNT(*) n FROM order_fact WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) o ON o.d=c.d LEFT JOIN (SELECT date(created_at) d, COUNT(*) n FROM tickets WHERE category='کالای معیوب' GROUP BY 1) t ON t.d=c.d

WITH dl AS (SELECT date(delivered_at) d, category, COUNT(*) n FROM order_fact WHERE delivered_at IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2), dm AS (SELECT date(t.created_at) d, o.category, COUNT(*) n FROM tickets t JOIN orders o USING(order_id) WHERE t.category='کالای معیوب' GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT c.d, dl.category dim, ROUND(100.0*COALESCE((SELECT SUM(n) FROM dm WHERE dm.category=dl.category AND dm.d BETWEEN date(c.d,'-6 day') AND c.d),0) /SUM(dl.n),2) value FROM cal c JOIN dl ON dl.d BETWEEN date(c.d,'-6 day') AND c.d GROUP BY c.d, dl.category

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.task_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN task_fact t ON t.team_id='T_WH' AND t.due_date < c.d AND date(t.created_at) <= c.d AND (t.done_at IS NULL OR date(t.done_at) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.task_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN task_fact t ON t.team_id='T_SHP' AND t.due_date < c.d AND date(t.created_at) <= c.d AND (t.done_at IS NULL OR date(t.done_at) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d
SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.ticket_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN tickets t ON date(t.created_at)=c.d GROUP BY c.d
SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.ticket_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN ticket_fact t ON t.created_at <= c.d||' 22:00:00' AND (t.resolved_at IS NULL OR t.resolved_at > c.d||' 22:00:00') GROUP BY c.d
SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.ticket_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN tickets t ON date(t.created_at)=c.d AND t.team_id='T_RSP' GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.ticket_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN ticket_fact t ON t.team_id='T_RSP' AND t.created_at <= c.d||' 22:00:00' AND (t.first_response_at IS NULL OR t.first_response_at > c.d||' 22:00:00') GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.task_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN task_fact t ON t.team_id='T_RSP' AND t.due_date < c.d AND date(t.created_at) <= c.d AND (t.done_at IS NULL OR date(t.done_at) > c.d) GROUP BY c.d
SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.ticket_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN tickets t ON date(t.created_at)=c.d AND t.team_id='T_CMP' GROUP BY c.d

SELECT c.d, COUNT(t.ticket_id) value FROM cal c LEFT JOIN ticket_fact t ON t.team_id='T_CMP' AND t.created_at <= c.d||' 22:00:00' AND (t.resolved_at IS NULL OR t.resolved_at > c.d||' 22:00:00') GROUP BY c.d

gross_raw.sql: SELECT SUM(o.order_value_toman) FROM orders o JOIN order_events e USING(order_id) WHERE e.event='paid'

gross_distinct.sql: SELECT SUM(o.order_value_toman) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM orders) o JOIN order_events e USING(order_id) WHERE e.event='paid'

joined_rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders LEFT JOIN order_events USING(order_id)

joined_rows_distinct.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM orders) LEFT JOIN order_events USING(order_id)

order_fact_rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT o.*, MAX(CASE WHEN e.event='paid' THEN e.at END) paid_at FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_events e USING(order_id) GROUP BY o.order_id)

b2c_net_raw.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN e.event='paid' THEN o.order_value_toman ELSE -e.amount_toman END) FROM order_events e JOIN orders o USING(order_id) WHERE e.event IN ('paid','refunded')

b2c_net_distinct.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN e.event='paid' THEN o.order_value_toman ELSE -e.amount_toman END) FROM order_events e JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT * FROM orders) o USING(order_id) WHERE e.event IN ('paid','refunded')
